name: Bhavyy Khurana
project_details: Hopfield Networks with Adaptive Memory and Dynamic Pattern Forgetting: Built a Hopfield-network variant that resists memory degradation under interference by adding feedback-driven adaptive forgetting, proposed as Adaptive Hopfield Memory (AHM-DPF). Improved recall accuracy by 25-33 percentage points over classical Hopfield baselines under high-interference regimes on a purpose-built bit-pattern benchmark (8-D to 64-D).

Adversarial Robustness of Network Intrusion Detection Systems: Built a DNN-based NIDS on UNSW-NB15 achieving a weighted F1 of 0.709. Evaluated adversarial robustness under FGSM & PGD attacks; exposed 81.7% macro-F1 collapse and a degenerate prediction artifact that inflated robustness estimates in prior work.

Network Intrusion Anomaly Detection System GitHub: Built a hybrid intrusion detection pipeline combining a supervised Random Forest layer for known threats with unsupervised One-Class SVM for zero-day attack detection. Achieved 0.858 ROC-AUC for zero-day detection, with the supervised layer evaluated using imbalance-aware metrics on the heavily class-imbalanced UNSW-NB15 dataset.
education: B.Tech in Computer Science Engineering (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning) at Manipal Institute of Technology
work_exp: Data and Analytics Intern at Lepton Software (2026)
internship_details: Built a sub-hourly nowcasting pipeline to predict rainfall-driven traffic disruption, combining live persistence with GAN-downscaled 2km precipitation fields for short-horizon road impact forecasting. Designed and maintained the geospatial data layer by integrating ERA5 reanalysis, Google Weather API forecasts, and road-network mappings using H3 spatial indexing, PostGIS, and PostgreSQL.
